entries.title: Python September releases fix security issues and move 3.13 to security-only support
entries.summary: Python 3.14.8 and 3.12.15 address security issues involving TLS and archive handling; 3.13.16 is the final full maintenance release of the 3.13 series. This September 30 release cycle matters for research environments that process external files and for planning maintenance of pinned Python versions. Subsequent Python 3.13 releases will contain security fixes only.

entries.title: renv 1.3.0 hardens Git restoration and improves reproducibility
entries.summary: renv 1.3.0 tightens handling of Git URLs, refs, and commits to prevent crafted package records from triggering unintended commands. It also records resolved Git commits and improves transactional restore retries, helping teams recreate the same R environment more reliably.

entries.title: uv September updates improve package integrity and environment checks
entries.summary: uv 0.12.18 fixes a Windows wheel-installation path traversal weakness and adds read-only environment checks with JSON output. Related September releases add signed macOS/Windows binaries and strengthen repeated-requirement hash checks and recovery after interrupted project changes. These changes support safer, auditable Python environment management.

entries.title: RStudio 2026.09 adds split source views and managed Assistant controls
entries.summary: RStudio 2026.09.0 adds horizontal and vertical source-editor splits that share edits while allowing independent navigation. It also adds controls for administrator-managed Posit Assistant installations, helping teams review long analysis scripts and maintain consistent tooling. Separate Workbench-only features should not be assumed available in the open-source IDE.

entries.title: VS Code 1.136.2 addresses agent and workspace security issues
entries.summary: VS Code 1.136.2 is a security update covering issues in agent network filtering, remote agent connections, workspace restrictions, and related components. Teams using coding agents or external repositories should include this release in their editor security review.

entries.title: VS Code September updates bring agent sessions into development containers
entries.summary: VS Code 1.138 adds local Dev Container agent sessions and expanded Codex integration; 1.139 extends container sessions to SSH, Tunnel, and WSL hosts. Version 1.140 adds a Copilot harness and enterprise AI controls, while multi-folder sessions and shared worktree folders remain experimental. Together these changes help coding agents use project-specific dependencies across local and remote environments.
entries.channel: stable release with explicitly labeled experimental features

entries.title: DuckDB 1.5.6 fixes analytical query correctness and recovery issues
entries.summary: DuckDB 1.5.6 fixes incorrect results involving Top-N window optimizations, NULL ordering, and timezone state during timestamp parsing. It also addresses duplicate output chunks and failed multi-statement rollback paths, making this maintenance release relevant to reliable SQL-based research analysis.

entries.title: nf-core/rnaseq 3.27.0 expands screening and restores strandedness handling
entries.summary: nf-core/rnaseq 3.27.0 adds raw or trimmed-read contamination screening and support for prebuilt Bowtie2 rRNA indexes. It restores StringTie strandedness flags and fixes failures involving Azure indexes, NCBI annotations, and kallisto-only runs. The pipeline now requires Nextflow 25.10.4 or newer, which matters when updating reproducible RNA-seq workflows.

entries.title: Ruff 0.16.8 improves autofix safety and Python compatibility
entries.summary: Ruff 0.16.8 preserves operand order in SIM109 fixes and required parentheses in multiline UP040 conversions, and marks UP040 fixes as unsafe. These changes matter when automated linting edits analysis code, where apparently small rewrites can change behavior; the release also extends Python 3.15 compatibility.

entries.title: GPT-6 Sol, Luna, and GPT-6.1 Sol arrive in Codex and ChatGPT Work
entries.summary: September brought GPT-6 Sol and Luna, followed by GPT-6.1 Sol, to Codex and ChatGPT Work. Model choices for coding and document workflows depend on rollout, plan, client, and workspace settings; these announcements do not establish availability in Chat.

entries.title: OpenAI desktop macOS update fixes CVE-2026-100754
entries.summary: The September 25 desktop changelog reports a macOS security fix in version 26.924.20706. This is relevant to teams maintaining ChatGPT/Codex desktop installations; the announcement gives no technical vulnerability details.

entries.title: Codex removes its MCP server command
entries.summary: The September 5 release removes the codex mcp-server command and standalone binary. Integrations using that interface need revision; external MCP connections remain supported, while app-server is experimental.

entries.title: September model notices require Codex configuration changes
entries.summary: GPT-5.3-Codex-Spark became unavailable on September 14; a separate notice announced GPT-5.5 retirement from ChatGPT, Work, and Codex for October 14. Teams should update saved model selections; the GPT-5.5 notice excludes the API.

entries.title: ChatGPT adds shared Spaces and synced Work tasks
entries.summary: The September 29 announcement introduces ChatGPT Space for files, Pages, and collaboration, alongside new Work tasks that sync across desktop, web, and mobile. Local-file operations still require an online connected computer, and existing tasks retain their original mode.

entries.title: Codex introduces reusable cloud development environments
entries.summary: Codex can prepare and test a development environment, then reuse its filesystem in isolated cloud workspaces. Announced September 29, this supports repeatable coding tasks that continue while the local computer sleeps.

entries.title: Claude September model releases expand coding and analysis options
entries.summary: Claude Code added Fable 5.1 on September 1, Opus 5.5 on September 22, and Sonnet 5.5 on September 28. Anthropic positions Opus for complex work and Sonnet for faster focused tasks; performance claims remain vendor evaluations. API integrations should check migration requirements, including changes to thinking controls and preserved conversation context.
entries.channel: model releases; Claude Code availability independently verified

entries.title: Claude combines Cowork and chat with document and slide editing
entries.summary: Anthropic began merging Cowork and chat on September 16, initially rolling out to Pro and Max users across web, desktop, and mobile. The announcement also introduced Docs and Slides and in-conversation Design as paid-plan betas, with Enterprise administrator controls. This brings drafting, editing, and longer-running report work into a shared conversation.

entries.title: Claude Code September updates add evaluations and tighter permission controls
entries.summary: September Claude Code releases add reproducible plugin evaluations and a prompt audit for instructions written for older models. Managed model allow/deny controls and permission fixes support more consistent agent use, while a late-month fix prevents session-resume failures from losing parallel tool-call history. These are grouped workflow and reliability updates rather than separate entries for each daily patch.
